items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: And then Thelonious said, "Come on down," and we with Trane and Shadow went down there, and we played -- and that was the gig.

ctx.x: No rehearsal. We just went up there and played. But it was good gigs, you know? That was around '68. All the

while, Clifford Jordan is hooking up a tour of Europe he wants me to go on. He called me from Europe. He left and went over there. He called me, "Many they wanted a brochure on you and he got a string of gigs over here. Told me the price and all that. I wasn't ready for it, so I wouldn't go. I'm still working in New York around this time. Eddie Blackwell came by my house. He stayed right around the corner from me. He said, "Man, Monk wants you to work with us." So, that was a joy, to work with the T again, openly…

Monk, Blackwell, Charlie Rouse (PHONETIC) and I think that was the last time Charlie worked with T. Thelonius was kind of ill and he was saying things that really hurt Charles' feelings, but we made the weekend -- no, we made that week and then Monk went into the hospital. This was all '68 mostly. And I'm working down at Slugs with different little groups and I worked with Sonny Rollins down at the Vanguard. Al Foster, Al Daley (PHONETIC), myself.
